security_audit.summary: All 56 static findings are false positives involving Markdown backticks, Cloudflare documentation links, descriptive metadata, or account authentication checks. No evidence found of prompt injection, unauthorized data exfiltration, or malicious device access. The skill documents authenticated operations and explicitly warns about destructive flags and migration risks; the external CLI implementation was not audited.

content.user_title: Manage Cloudflare Resources with the cf CLI
content.value_statement: Cloudflare command discovery and mixed Wrangler projects can make terminal workflows difficult to verify. This skill guides command lookup, request previews, authentication, and project-aware execution.
actual_capabilities: Guide task-based command discovery with cf cli search, API schema inspection, and command help.
Explain installation prerequisites, CLI name collisions, browser sign-in, and token authentication for CI.
Guide request previews and identify destructive force flags and misleading delete exit codes.
Select cf or Wrangler workflows based on existing project configuration and user-requested migration.
Explain JSON output, standard error handling, pagination, and limited local-mode support.
Document Wrangler fallbacks for Worker logs and single-secret provisioning.
limitations: The cf CLI is in beta; commands, configuration, and build output can change.
Execution requires an installed CLI and Node.js 22.18 or later; Bun is not supported.
Remote resource operations require suitable credentials; unattended agents cannot complete interactive sign-in.
Not every Wrangler command or local operation is supported; help and current documentation remain necessary.

use_cases.title: Discover a resource command
use_cases.description: Find a DNS management command, inspect its required arguments, and preview the request before changing a resource.

use_cases.title: Preserve an existing Workers workflow
use_cases.description: Check project configuration and retain Wrangler development workflows unless migration is explicitly requested.

use_cases.title: Prepare unattended operations
use_cases.description: Plan token authentication, request previews, and output checks for Cloudflare commands in a non-interactive environment.

prompt_templates.title: Check CLI readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the cf installation prerequisites and how to check its version and authentication status. Do not install packages or begin sign-in.

prompt_templates.title: Find and preview a DNS command
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the cf command for creating a DNS record. Inspect its schema and help, then prepare a dry-run using placeholders without changing resources.

prompt_templates.title: Choose the project workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect this project for Cloudflare and Wrangler configuration. Recommend the correct development CLI and explain migration considerations without modifying files.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: evaluate an existing Workers project.

prompt_templates.title: Review a non-interactive operation
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this proposed cf deletion workflow for CI. Check authentication, dry-run support, force semantics, stderr, and aborted-delete handling without executing it.

output_examples.input: Which CLI should I use when this project only has Wrangler configuration?
output: Keep Wrangler for development, builds, and deployment.
Cloudflare resource commands can run alongside the existing workflow.
Migrate only after an explicit request and a migration preview.

output_examples.input: A non-interactive delete exited successfully but printed Aborted. Was the resource deleted?
output: A zero exit code does not prove deletion; an aborted destructive command can also exit zero.
Check standard error and verify the resource state.
Review the command schema and force behavior before retrying.

output_examples.input: How can an unattended CI job authenticate with cf?
output: Use CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN rather than interactive browser login.
Supply the token through protected CI secrets with permissions limited to the required operations.
Check command help and preview the request before running resource changes.

best_practices: Discover commands with search, inspect schema and help, and preview unfamiliar requests before execution.
Respect existing project configuration and obtain explicit approval before migration or destructive changes.
Protect CI tokens, review force flags, and verify stderr and resource state rather than relying only on exit codes.
anti_patterns: Guessing cf equivalents from remembered Wrangler commands without consulting search or documentation.
Running cf project lifecycle commands in a Wrangler-only project without an approved migration.
Treating a zero delete exit code as success or adding force flags without checking their API effects.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The skill supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Command execution still depends on the tool environment and its permissions.

faq.question: What runtime does cf require?
faq.answer: The documented minimum is Node.js 22.18. Bun is not supported, and the CLI must be installed separately.

faq.question: Can CI use interactive sign-in?
faq.answer: Unattended CI cannot complete cf auth login. Use CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN through protected secret storage instead.

faq.question: Does cf replace every Wrangler command?
faq.answer: No. The skill documents Wrangler fallbacks for live logs and single-secret provisioning, and points to the current compatibility reference.

faq.question: Does dry-run change remote resources?
faq.answer: The documented dry-run prints the request without sending it and requires no credentials. Confirm support using the selected command help.

faq.question: Does local mode work for every resource command?
faq.answer: No. Local mode supports selected KV, D1, and R2 operations. Unsupported commands, including cf d1 query, return an error.
